# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

I can see the display reads 0, the light is yellow, and there are three wires in order green, yellow, blue. Mute’s two-thumbs-up gesture has no established meaning for me yet, so I will relay the observable bomb state verbally to both hearing monkeys.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is yellow. Three wires, ordered 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The display and wire order are unchanged, but the light has changed from yellow to orange. Mute’s single raised finger may be intended as a numeric instruction, but no gesture code has been established, so I should report the visible change and ask for an unambiguous verbal/gesture-supported instruction for Blind.

``` 
speak(text="Update: display still 0; wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light has changed from yellow to orange. I received your single-finger gesture but do not know its meaning. Please indicate the required action clearly for Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ 👍]

The light is now green; display 0 and the green/yellow/blue wire order remain unchanged. Mute’s gesture sequence is still not an established code for me, so I cannot safely convert it into an instruction. I will update Blind with the visible state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb view: display 0; light green; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute has sent gestures, but their meaning is not established, so do not act on them yet.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has returned to yellow; the display remains 0 and the wire order is still green, yellow, blue. Since no intelligible action instruction has reached me, I will report the current state and continue to tell Blind not to act without a verified instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. No verified instruction yet; do not act.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light is orange again, with display 0 and wires green/yellow/blue in positions 1/2/3. Mute has now signalled an upright index finger followed by a thumbs-up, which most plausibly indicates wire 1 as the selected/approved wire. Blind’s 1–2–3 gesture appears to request a wire number. I will give Blind the state and relay that likely instruction, explicitly noting the uncertainty.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0; orange light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signalled an upright index finger followed by thumbs-up, plausibly approving/selecting wire 1. This is not fully verified; use your manual-derived confirmation if available before acting.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light is green again; display 0 and the wire order remain green, yellow, blue. Blind is repeating a 1–2–3 gesture sequence, likely requesting a wire-selection instruction. Mute’s current visible signal is an open palm, which I can faithfully relay as “five,” but its operational meaning is not known to me. I should provide Blind both the current state and that exact relay rather than guessing an action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: display 0; light green; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's latest gesture is an open hand/palm, i.e. five. I do not know what action that code denotes.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is yellow again; display remains 0 and wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again made the same open-palm gesture as last turn. Rather than infer an unsafe wire choice, I will give Blind the complete observed light/gesture sequence so they can combine it with their tactile controls and any protocol they have inferred.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current view: display 0; yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Full Mute-gesture timeline by light: yellow: two thumbs-up; orange: raised index; green: open palm, raised index, thumbs-up; yellow: none; orange: raised index, thumbs-up; green: open palm; yellow now: open palm. I cannot safely decode the gesture code.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb remains at display 0 with wires green, yellow, blue in positions 1–3, and its light is now orange. Mute has again signalled a raised index finger. Blind previously asked for a 1–2–3 wire designation, so this is most likely Mute’s answer: wire 1.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Now: orange light, display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute signals raised index finger again: likely select wire 1 (green).")
```
